Salt Self Defense Gun - Shaped like a traditional handgun, it shoots rounds filled with a powdered mix of chemicals that create a toxic cloud upon impact, incapacitating anyone in the vicinity.

If I was the victim of a home invasion, and I had access to a firearm, I'd much rather have actual bullets. Because while salt rounds do cause "respiratory and visual distress," even when they are effective, you still have an intruder in your house who is technically conscious and can potenially still harm you.

Non-lethal, incapacitating tools have been around for a long time. They have obvious police and military application and a lot of attention has been devoted to developing them.

The best we currently have are tasers and paper spray.

The problem is that incapacitation is really hard. Consider something simple - a punch to the gut. If an ordinary middle-aged guy walks up to an unsuspecting stranger and punches him hard in the gut, the chances are excellent the stranger is going down. But this same ordinary guy would probably have his ass handed to him if he tried to use the same gut punch to ward off an attacker.

A handful of salty powder might be better than nothing, but it is nothing to bet you life on. If firearms are not an option, get the best pepper spray you can find. It's been in use for many years and it's been used many thousands of times in real life, and it's known to be the best chemical option available. There is avery little likelihood that this stuff will supersede it.
